speaker: Doctor
text: How old are you, and where exactly is the pain located when you try to walk?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Is the pain in your knee sharp or a dull ache, and does it happen all the time or only when you walk?  
REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP (to check for infection/inflammation).

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is incorrect; a pediatric patient with knee pain and a limp but no fever cannot have a migraine. I need to know if the pain radiates from your hip into the knee, and I must request an X-Ray of the left hip to rule out Perthes disease.

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray of the left hip (AP and Frog-leg lateral views).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the left hip shows flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.
